tagline: A ranch-country loop where the outlaw had only a supporting role.
intro: Out of Ruidoso, a mountain resort town named for its noisy creek, the loop runs north through Alto to Capitan, then east past Fort Stanton to Lincoln in the Bonito Valley. At Hondo the Rio Bonito and the Rio Ruidoso join, and the road turns back west up the Ruidoso through San Patricio. It is 84 miles around, by grassland and pine forest in the Lincoln National Forest.

Hispanic families settled these valleys in the 1850s and built placitas, adobe compounds walled for defense. The Lincoln County War came later, two factions fighting over government contracts. Billy the Kid had only a supporting role in it. The road is named for him all the same.

moments.title: Capitan
moments.text: In spring 1950 a badly burned bear cub was rescued from a fire at Capitan Gap and became the living Smokey Bear. After 26 years at the National Zoo he came home for burial.

moments.title: Fort Stanton
moments.text: Built in 1855 for campaigns against the Mescalero Apache, the fort was home at one time or another to Kit Carson, Buffalo Soldiers of the 9th Cavalry, Billy the Kid and Pat Garrett.

moments.title: Lincoln
moments.text: The village's only street is US 380. In April 1881 Billy the Kid, held at the courthouse under sentence of hanging, killed both his guards and rode out on a stolen horse.
